definitions: The imaginary 'wall' at the front of the stage in a traditional three-walled box set in a proscenium arch theatre, which separates the actors from the audience.
The conceptual barrier between any fictional work or character and its audience or reader.
examples: Breaking the fourth wall can be a powerful dramatic device.
The comedian often shattered the fourth wall with direct address to the audience.
Many modern plays experiment with the fourth wall.
